1392.6: Swayye in praise of the Third Guru (Guru Amar Das Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Remember that True Being, whose one Name is beyond all deceit in the world. Remember that same supreme Name, which has carried the devotees across the world-ocean. (Guru) Nanak delights in that Name; in it Lahna was established, and through it (came) all the siddhis (miraculous powers). O humble poet Kal, the glory of (Guru) Amar Das, wise of understanding, has spread among the people. His glory has shone out across the world like the rays of the sun, (spreading its fragrance) like the branches of the noble maulsari tree. In the north, the south, the east and the west, people hail his victory. The Lord's Name, uttered by the tongue, was given out through the Guru, and the Ganga was turned back and set flowing west: That same Name, beyond all deceit, which carries the devotees across the world-ocean, has been revealed within Guru Amar Das. ॥1॥
The Ganga flows east; to turn it west is an image of the mind turned back from the world. Maulsari: a tree with small, sweet-scented flowers.
1393.1: The Jakhs and the Kinnars, the seekers and the Siddhas, and Shiva in samadhi remember that same Name. The stars and the realm of Dhru remember it, and the great ones besides, Narad, Prahlad and others. The moon and the sun yearn for the Name, by which even rocks and mountains have been carried across. That same Name, beyond all deceit, which carries the devotees across the world-ocean, has been revealed within Guru Amar Das. ॥2॥
Jakhs (Yakshas) and Kinnars: classes of demigods in the Puranas. Narad is a sage of the Puranas, messenger of the gods and a devotee of Vishnu.
1393.2: Remembering that same Name of the Immaculate One, the nine Naths, Shiva, and Sanak and the others were saved. Steeped in it are the eighty-four Siddhas and the wise; by it Ambrik crossed the world-ocean. Udho, Akrur, Tilochan and Nama (remembered it), and in the Kalyug it took away Kabir's sins. That same Name, beyond all deceit, which carries the devotees across the world-ocean, has been revealed within Guru Amar Das. ॥3॥
The eighty-four Siddhas are held to be the masters of the yogis' tradition. Ambrik is a devotee king of the Puranas.
1393.3: Attached to that Name, the thirty-three (crore gods) meditate; it dwells in the minds of the celibates and the great ascetics. Remembering that same Name, his mind on (the Lord's) feet, Gangev Pitamah tasted the Amrit. Joined to that Name through the Guru, profound and deep in understanding, the Sangat, holding (it) true, is saved. That same Name, beyond all deceit, which carries the devotees across the world-ocean, has been revealed within Guru Amar Das. ॥4॥
Gangev Pitamah: Bhishma, son of the Ganga, the grandsire of the Mahabharata.
1393.4: The glory of the Name (spreads) through the world like the rays of the sun, like the branches of the tree of heaven. In the lands of the north, the south, the east and the west, (people) speak its praise. This life is fruitful only when the Lord's Name comes to dwell in the heart. The gods, men, the ganas, the Gandharbs and the six orders (of ascetics) long for it. On the renowned Bhalla, the son of Tej (Bhan), Kal has meditated with palms joined: O Guru Amar Das, you have obtained that same Name, which ends the world-ocean for the devotees. ॥5॥
Gandharbs: the singers of the gods. Tej Bhan was Guru Amar Das Ji's father. Bhalla is a clan: Guru Amar Das Ji was a Bhalla.
1393.5: The thirty-three (crore) gods, the seekers, the Siddhas and men meditate on the Name; the Name upholds the continents and the universes. Those who have meditated on the Name have borne joy and sorrow alike. The Name of the all-pervading (Lord) is supreme; the devotees dwell (in it), their attention fixed. O Guru Amar (Das), the Creator, well pleased, has given (you) that same treasure, the Name. ॥6॥
1393.6: (Guru Amar Das) is a hero of truth, strong in gentleness and in a tranquil nature; his Sangat is vast, his understanding deep, and he is absorbed in the One without enmity. His patience, from the very beginning, is the white banner set up on the bridge to Baikunth (heaven). The Sants touch (the feet of) him, love itself, who is united with the Creator. Serving the True Guru, (they) have found peace; Guru Amar (Das) has made (them) worthy. ॥7॥
1393.7: (For him) the Name is his bathing (at the tiraths), the Name his tasty food and his meal; the relish of the Name is his constant delight, and sweet words are in his mouth. Blessed is the True Guru whom he served, by whose grace he came to know the state of the Unreachable One. Whole lineages have been saved; he has found the Name dwelling (within him). Kal says: fruitful is the life of him who has touched Guru Amar (Das), the light made manifest. ॥8॥
1394.1: In his right hand is (the mark of) the lotus; siddhi stands before him, watching his face. At his left side dwells riddhi (wealth), which enchants the three worlds. In his heart dwells the Indescribable One; he alone has known that joy. Imbued with this love, Guru Amar (Das) utters devotion with his mouth. On his forehead is the true mark of (God's) grace; Kal has meditated on him with palms joined. He who has touched the Guru, the crown of True Gurus, has obtained all he desires. ॥9॥
The mark of a lotus on the palm is held to be the sign of a great soul.
1394.2: Truly fruitful are the feet, the feet that walk the path of Guru Amar (Das). Truly fruitful are the hands, the hands that touch the feet of Guru Amar (Das). Truly fruitful is the tongue, the tongue with which Guru Amar (Das) is praised. Truly fruitful are the eyes, the eyes with which Guru Amar (Das) is seen. Truly fruitful are the ears, the ears with which Guru Amar (Das) is heard. Fruitful is that heart in which dwells Guru Amar Das, the very father of the world. Jalap says: fruitful is that head, the head that ever bows to Guru Amar (Das). ॥1॥
Jalap (also Jal) too is one of the Bhatts.
1394.3: Those men know no sorrow and no hunger; those men are never called poor. Grief does not come upon those men; the end of those men cannot be found. Those men serve no one; those men give away hundreds and thousands. Those men sit on carpets (of honour); those men unseat (some) and establish (others). Those men find peace in the world; amid enemies they wear the robe of fearlessness. Jalap says: fruitful are those men with whom Guru Amar Das is well pleased. ॥2॥
1394.4: (O Guru Amar Das,) you have read of the One, held the One in your mind, and known the One as the only One. In your eyes, in your words, in your mouth is the One, the One alone; you have known no duality anywhere. In dreams the One, awake the One; you are absorbed in the One. The One, who is the same through the thirty (days of the month), manifest in the five (elements), and undying in the thirty-five (letters of the Bani); the One from whom come the lakhs (of beings), and who is beyond the grasp of the lakhs: him you have described as One, the only One. Jalap says: O Guru Amar Das, you long for the One and believe in the One. ॥3॥
1394.5: The understanding Jaidev grasped, the understanding that dwelt in Nama, the understanding in Trilochan's mind, which Bhagat Kabir knew; (by which) Rukmangad's practice was (to say): O brothers, ever repeat Ram; (by which) Ambrik and Prahlad, in Gobind's refuge, attained the supreme state: (O Guru,) you have given up greed, anger and craving; you have known, (says) Jal, the way of that understanding. Guru Amar Das is (God's) own devotee; beholding him, I attain liberation. ॥4॥
Rukmangad is a devotee king of the Puranas, who had his people too repeat God's Name.
1394.6: Let us touch Guru Amar Das: the sins of the earth are destroyed. Let us touch Guru Amar Das: the Siddhas and the seekers long (for this). Let us touch Guru Amar Das: meditation (on God) is attained, and the journeys (of birth and death) end. Let us touch Guru Amar Das: the Fearless One is found, and the round (of births) is over. Recognising the One, the sense of a second goes only when men take to the sublime mantra (of the Guru). O Jalap, all these blessings are found by beholding Guru Amar Das. ॥5॥
1395.1: (Guru) Nanak firmly took to heart the True Name of the Creator. From him Lahna was revealed as (Guru) Angad, whose attention stayed on his feet. In that line is Guru Amar Das, the home of (all) hopes: which of his virtues can I describe? His virtues are beyond knowing and beyond reach; I do not know the end of those virtues. The Creator has made him a ship to carry across the whole Sangat and (their) lineages. Kirat says: O Guru Amar Das, save me, save me; I have come to the refuge of your feet. ॥1॥
Kirat too is one of the Bhatts.
1395.2: Narayan himself, taking on his power, has come forth into the world. The Formless One has given his light a form in the world. Everywhere the Shabad is fully present; with the lamp (of the Guru) he has made it shine. The Sikhs who have taken in its essence, (the Guru) has joined to the Lord's feet. Pure, he has been born in the line of (Guru) Nanak, having been with Angad, who was Lahna. O Guru Amar Das, the boat that carries across, birth after birth (I seek) the refuge of your feet. ॥2॥
1395.3: Beholding the Guru, his Sikhs gain meditation, austerity, truth and contentment. Those who fall into his refuge are saved, leaving behind the record of the city of Jam. His heart full of loving devotion, he utters (the praise of) the Creator. The Guru is a river full of pearls; he brings those who are drowning safe across in a moment. Pure, he has been born in the line of (Guru) Nanak, and he utters the Creator's virtues. Those who have served Guru Amar Das: sorrow and poverty flee far from them. ॥3॥
1395.4: I think in my mind to say a prayer, but I cannot even say it. All my cares are with you; my eyes are on the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy). If by your command the seal (of approval) is set, then I may serve the Master. When the Guru looks with his kindly glance, the Creator's Name (comes like) fruit to the mouth. O Unreachable, Unknowable Being, Cause (of all), whatever you command, that I say. O Guru Amar Das, Maker of all, as you keep me, so I live. ॥4॥
1395.5: Swayye of Bhikha. The Guru is (divine) knowledge and meditation; he joins (his) essence with the Essence. (Joined) to the True One, he is to be known as true; with a single mind he fixes his attention (on him). He keeps lust and anger under control; his mind, (restless as) the wind, does not fly off and run about. He dwells in the land of the Formless One; understanding (his) command, he attains (true) wisdom. In the Kalyug (the Guru) is the form of the Creator; only he who made (all this) knows (it). Bhikha says: I have met that Guru, who in the joy of Sahaj has given me his sight. ॥1॥
Bhikha too is one of the Bhatts.
1395.6: I have grown weary searching for Sants; I have seen a great many Saadhs, sannyasis, ascetics, and these pandits sweet of tongue. For a whole year I wandered, but no one won my trust. I heard the talk of those who talk, but no one's way of living pleased me. They have left the Lord's Name and are attached to another: what virtues of theirs can I tell? God has brought me, Bhikha, to meet the Guru: (O Guru,) as you keep me, so I live. ॥2॥
1396.1: Wearing the armour of samadhi, (the Guru) has mounted and taken his seat on the horse of (divine) knowledge. He has taken the bow of righteousness in his hands, and fought with the arrow of a devotee's gentleness. In the fear (of God) he is fearless; through the Guru's Shabad he has planted in his mind the spear of the unshakable Lord. He has cut to pieces the five fiends: lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride. O son of Tej (Bhan), crown of the Bhallas, by (Guru) Nanak's blessing you are the master of kings. Sal speaks the truth: O Guru Amar Das, by fighting thus you have conquered the army (of the passions). ॥1॥
Sal too is one of the Bhatts.
1396.2: The drops of the clouds, the hair of the earth (its plants), the flowers of spring cannot be counted; who can find the end of the sun's and the moon's rays, the ocean's depths, the Ganga's waves? With meditation like Rudra's (Shiva's) and the wisdom of the True Guru, O humble poet Bhal, one might perhaps tell of them; (but) your virtues, O Amar Das of the Bhallas, (cannot be told): you alone are your own likeness. ॥1॥
Bhal too is one of the Bhatts.
